Hi all,


I have this head scratching problem that needs your expertise. It’s about one of the same measures (i.e., likert scale with 5 categories) that I’ve been posting about in the past couple of weeks.  I wanted to use estimator of WLSMV in my CFA model.


I ran the CFA within lavaan using two approaches that I thought should produce identical results, but they did not. This makes me question whether my assumptions about how I specified my model were incorrect.  


Approach 1:  My original dataset is a likert scale measure with 42 items, with responses that range to 1 to 5.  The class data type for each variable was coded in the dataset as “numeric”.  According to this page here, http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html, if I simply specified all of my items as ordered factors, such as the following: 

df <- as.data.frame(apply, df, ordered)) #this transforms all of my numerical variables into ordered factors, i.e., ordinal variables

fit <- cfa(cfa.df, data=df)  #where cfa.df is an object in which I specified which items go with which factors (not shown)

 

Then, my understanding is that lavaan will automatically switch to WLSMV estimator:  It will use diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS) to estimate the model parameters, but it will use the full weight matrix to compute robust standard errors, and a mean-and variance adjusted test statistic.  Okay, sounds fine.  


Approach 2:  I leave my original dataset alone, with all variables’ class types specified as numeric.  And the only change is this:

df=data (where all 42 variables were coded as numeric)

fit <- cfa(cfa.df, data=df, estimator=“WLSMV”).  


I thought that the output of the two approaches should yield identical results, but I received different results. For example, even though the degrees of freedom for the specified model and baseline models were identical across both approaches, I saw that the number of free parameters was 154 for approach 1 and 112 for approach 2 so perhaps it refers to 42 thresholds approach #1 estimates that approach #2 did not??)   What did I do differently for both approaches and which one is the correct way of specifying WLSMV for my CFA model?  I noticed that after the global fit indices, output#1 also generated thresholds data, whereas output #2 did not, which makes me suspect that the syntax for my approach #1 was correct.  But I need someone to confirm and explain this please. Thank you so much!

parts: It's not clear to me what you think I did wrong.  Can you clarify?

You second message stated you made a typo, but your "correction" was still incorrect:

df <- as.data.frame(lapply, df, ordered)) # this should fail, because "lapply" is a function, not a matrix-like object

fit <- cfa (cfa.df, data=df, 
            ordered=c("item 1", "item 2", "item 3", ... "item 42))

That's correct, and should work fine.  And it should yield the same results as approach 1, if you use lapply() correctly:

df <- as.data.frame(lapply(df, ordered))
Anyway, would you say that I specified WLSMV correctly in my approach #1, versus approach #2?

Your approach 2 was incorrect because you simply requested the estimator="WLSMV" even though your indicators would be treated as numeric (continuous).  Using the ordered= argument will already trigger lavaan to set estimator="WLSMV" by default.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: 2 approaches that were thought to yield identical CFA results but did not.  Please advise.
parts: I don't think they're fixed for identification because the variance estimates are different for each item and each factor.

They are neither estimated nor fixed when parameterization = "delta" (the default); they are not model parameters at all.  The residual variances are implied by the facts that (a) the total SD is fixed to 1 (visible under Scales y* in the summary() output) and (b) the common-factor variance and factor loading implies what proportion of the latent item-responses (unknown) variance is due to the common factor (visible via setting summary(..., rsquare = TRUE)).

But what I don't understand is how come all the items and factors have the variances' estimates, but only the 8 factors have the values for std.err, z-value, and p value, whereas the 42 items have blanks for std.err, z-value, and p values?
Because the common-factor variances have been estimated, whereas the residual item variances are simply implied by other model parameters rather than estimated.
